articles.title: Jaypal Malviya Wins India's First Shooting Quota for the 2028 Olympics - GKToday
articles.content: Home Jaypal Malviya Wins India’s First Shooting Quota for the 2028 Olympics Jaypal Malviya Wins India’s First Shooting Quota for the 2028 Olympics Madhya Pradesh shooter Jaypal Malviya won a silver medal at the ISSF World Championship in Doha and secured India’s first shooting quota for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Malviya is from a village in Chhindwara district. Malviya used a second-hand pistol bought in 2022 with about ₹1 lakh borrowed from friends. He had made his international debut at a World Cup in Hangzhou in July 2026. The Olympic quota does not guarantee that he will represent India at the Games; selection trials will determine the team. Notable Points Championship schedule: The large World Shooting Championships have been held every four years since 1954. A separate shotgun championship began in 1934 and has been held biennially since 1959; shotgun events also have a separate World Championship in odd-numbered years. Changes to the event programme: Airgun events joined the championships in 1970 and the 10-metre running target in 1981. Junior competitions were added in 1994. In 2022, the ISSF held its first separate Rifle/Pistol World Championships, apart from Shotgun and Running Target events. articles.title: TVK Leaders Lobby For Trisha In Trichy East; Vijay's Advisors Push Rajya Sabha Route: Report
articles.content: Home News TVK Leaders Lobby For Trisha In Trichy East; Vijay’s Advisors Push Rajya... News State Tamil Nadu Actor Trisha Krishnan is reportedly being considered for a political entry through the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), with some party leaders pushing for her candidature from the Tiruchirappalli East Assembly constituency, as reported in Junior Vikatan. According to the report, certain sections within the TVK leadership have been pressing the party high command to field Trisha from Tiruchirappalli East. Preparations are allegedly already underway, with supporters reportedly undertaking discreet campaign activities in the constituency. The report also claims that an active campaign in favour of the TVK is taking place across churches in the constituency, ostensibly as part of efforts to build support ahead of a possible electoral contest involving the actor. However, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s advisors are said to favour a different political route for Trisha. They have reportedly suggested nominating her to the Rajya Sabha in the 2028 elections, when vacancies are expected to arise, thereby securing her entry into Parliament without contesting an Assembly election. Meanwhile, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) is also reportedly considering actor and Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) chief Kamal Haasan as a possible candidate from Tiruchirappalli East. According to the report, the DMK leadership approached Kamal Haasan to explore the possibility of fielding him in the constituency. However, Haasan, who is currently a Rajya Sabha MP, reportedly declined the proposal, stating that he was not interested in contesting any election. He is said to have offered instead to campaign extensively for the party during the by-election. Following his reluctance, the DMK leadership is reportedly considering renominating its sitting MLA, Inigo Irudayaraj, as its candidate. articles.title: Geothermal Energy: A New Chapter in India's Clean Energy Journey
articles.content: Opinion Geothermal Energy: A New Chapter in India’s Clean Energy Journey Geothermal energy is steady, low-carbon and not affected by weather. Unlike solar and wind, it is available throughout the year PIB SRINAGAR 11 Nov 2026 02:40 IST Follow Us Puga valley, a place located at 14,000 feet above sea level in southeastern Ladakh’s Chanthang is known for its hot springs and underground heat reserves. This place is completely redefining the geothermal story of the country. In July 2026, the ONGC Energy Centre commissioned the country's first two geothermal wells in the Puga valley. For a nation of 1.4 billion people that has long looked to the sun and wind for its renewable ambitions, the heat of the Earth itself is now entering daily conversations. The two wells, each 1,000 metres deep, will support reservoir evaluation. They also pave the way for India's first one-megawatt demonstration geothermal power project, marking the country's entry into geothermal power generation. Though the scale is modest, what it implies is more important. The concept of Geothermal Energy India is moving from resource assessment to field demonstration, and Puga valley is where that shift becomes visible. Geothermal energy is steady, low-carbon and not affected by weather. Unlike solar and wind, it is available throughout the year. This matters for a large, densely populated country that wants to add reliable, home-grown sources to its renewable energy mix. That is why regions like Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh become important. Science states why the Earth's interior is hot because it is driven by the radioactive decay of elements like “uranium, thorium and potassium”, along with residual heat from the planet's formation. In geologically active regions, faults and fractures let hot material travel closer to the surface, creating reservoirs of hot water and steam trapped within permeable rock. Deep wells bring these resources up. The steam drives a turbine connected to a generator, a process resembling conventional thermal power, except that naturally occurring underground heat replaces fuel combustion. The used water is condensed and reinjected into the reservoir, supporting replenishment and continued production. Importance of Puga What makes Ladakh's milestone critical is the policy framework behind it. In September 2025, the government notified the National Policy on Geothermal Energy. The policy aims to establish geothermal energy as a major renewable pillar enabling systematic exploration and deployment of the country's resources. While prioritising research, drilling, reservoir management and direct-use applications, and supports Ground Source Heat Pumps for heating and cooling. A clear regulatory framework encourages both public and private sector participation. It facilitates repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells, builds toward a national geothermal data repository, and supports pilot projects and Centres of Excellence. Alongside this, MNRE is implementing the Renewable Energy Research and Technology Development Programme through research institutions and industry partners, aiming at indigenous, cost-effective technologies.
